$schema-note: Dated + justified allowlist for the vinext PRE-COMPILE CLOSURE supply-chain gate (scripts/precompile-closure-audit.mjs, ADR-0042 C6 / #764). Mirrors security/npm-audit-allowlist.json and the Trivy triage discipline: an accepted HIGH/CRITICAL in the closure that feeds `vite build` is suppressed ONLY by an entry here, so the gate can never be silently neutered. Each entry MUST carry: `id` (a GHSA/CVE id), `justification` (why it is accepted — no fix available, not reachable in our usage, etc.), and `added` (ISO date). `expires` (ISO date) is optional; past its expiry the entry stops suppressing and the risk must be re-justified. `note` (free text) is the only other permitted key: an entry carrying any key outside [id, justification, added, expires, note] makes the gate THROW, because a misspelled `expires` would otherwise be silently ignored and the entry would never expire while reading as though it does. A malformed entry makes the gate THROW rather than be ignored. Bump the dependency FIRST (as nanoid 3.3.17 -> 3.3.18 was, via an override in examples/bun-exec/package.json); allowlist only when there is no fix. SCOPE, stated because it is a real widening: this ONE file backs BOTH closures the gate audits — `--closure examples/bun-exec` and `--app apps/file-manager` (C1/#785) — so an entry accepted for one suppresses the same advisory in the other. Every justification must therefore name the closure and the reachability argument it rests on, and an entry whose argument holds only for one closure must be re-examined, not renewed, if the other starts carrying the same package.

allow.justification: decode-uri-component 0.2.2 (quadratic-time DoS in percent-decoding; fixed only in 0.5.1, advisory range <= 0.5.0). Pulled ONLY via query-string@7.1.3 <- minio@8.0.6 <- @getknext/lib (runtime, bundled into the closure). The bump is NOT taken: 0.5.1 is ESM-only (type: module, default export) and query-string 7 require()s it expecting a CJS function, so `query-string.parse` throws `decodeComponent is not a function` (verified under node 24 and bun 1.4.2); minio 8.0.7 (latest) still pins query-string ^7.1.3, so no clean upgrade path exists. REACHABILITY: the decode path is reached only through query-string's parse/extract, and minio's dist calls only `qs.stringify` (internal/client.js, helpers.js) — no request or response bytes are ever decoded by this package. The module is loaded but its quadratic decode routine is never invoked. Applies identically to every closure that carries minio (apps/docs, apps/file-manager, the published @getknext/lib closure). Re-check at expiry: if minio moves to a query-string that pulls a fixed decode-uri-component, or query-string is replaced, bump and drop this entry rather than renewing it; if any code calls query-string.parse on untrusted input, this entry must be dropped and the path fixed. PATCH ROUTE considered and rejected: a bun patchedDependencies edit of query-string 7.1.3 (loading decode-uri-component's `.default`) only changes THIS repo's install; consumers of the published @getknext/lib resolve minio -> query-string -> decode-uri-component themselves, so the published closure would still carry 0.2.2, and the patch would fork a third-party package we then have to maintain. RE-CHECKED 2026-11-06 (renewal, 45 days): minio latest is still 8.0.7 and still depends on query-string ^7.1.3; query-string latest is 10.0.0 (ESM-only); decode-uri-component latest is 0.5.1 and is still "type": "module" with only an ESM `default` export, so query-string 7 cannot require() it; the 8.0.7 tarball's dist/main still calls only qs.stringify (internal/client.js x5, helpers.js x1) and never parse/parseUrl/extract. The advisory is unchanged (high, fixed in 0.5.1). Nothing has changed since acceptance except the clock.
